bug_semantics: The vulnerable product is the proprietary AIT CSV Import / Export WordPress plugin, not Metasploit. In plugin versions through 3.0.3, the directly web-reachable admin/upload-handler.php accepts an unauthenticated multipart file field without restricting the uploaded type. An attacker can submit a .php file; although the handler may report a CSV parse error, the file remains in wp-content/uploads and is web-executable, yielding unauthenticated remote code execution even when the plugin is installed but inactive. WPScan also reports possible deletion through the same handler.
flaw_origin: External proprietary AIT Themes plugin source at ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php. The assigned rapid7/metasploit-framework repository contains only a downstream exploit module that demonstrates the flaw; it does not contain the vulnerable plugin implementation or its release history.
ai_marker: Unavailable: the true BIC commit object for the proprietary AIT plugin is not present in the assigned repository or in known public source history, so no BIC-only author, committer, bot identity, or AI trailer can be inspected. The downstream Metasploit exploit-module commit object was deliberately not substituted for the BIC.
evidence: Alias resolution: https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-34083 reports that CVE-2025-34083 was rejected as a duplicate of CVE-2020-36849. The canonical record at https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2020-36849 identifies missing file-type validation in /wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php through version 3.0.3 and cites the Rapid7 file only as an exploit.

Attack path and disclosure: https://wpscan.com/vulnerability/36e699a4-91f2-426d-ba14-26036fbfeaea records an observed GET to the handler on 2020-11-12, a working exploit against then-current 3.0.3, public disclosure on 2020-11-13, and the reproducer `curl -F 'file=@plugin.php' http://HOST/wp-content/plugins/ait-csv-import-export/admin/upload-handler.php`; it explains that the malicious file remains uploaded despite CSV parsing.

Version boundary: https://www.wordfence.com/threat-intel/vulnerabilities/wordpress-plugins/ait-csv-import-export/ait-csv-importexport-303-arbitrary-file-upload lists affected versions `* <= 3.0.3`, patched version `* 3.0.4`, and remediation to update to 3.0.4 or newer. This is corroborated by the assigned clone's module target `AIT CSV Import Export <3.0.4` and its check against 3.0.4 in modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb.

Repository mismatch: in /home/hanqing/agents/ai-slop/.ai-slop/state/repos/rapid7_metasploit-framework, `git log --all --follow --format='%H %P %ad %an %s' -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` begins at d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 (parent a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d), dated 2021-01-01 with subject `ait csv improter exploit`, after the 2020 disclosure. `git show d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` shows a new 90-line Metasploit Ruby client that uploads a generated PHP payload to the plugin endpoint and then requests it from wp-content/uploads; it is exploit evidence, not the vulnerable PHP handler.

Downstream ancestry cross-check: `git log -S'upload-handler.php' -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` and `git log -L 76,90:modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb --format='%H %P %s' --no-patch` both identify only d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135 for the exploit request lines. `git ls-tree -r --name-only a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d -- modules/exploits/multi/http/wp_ait_csv_rce.rb` is empty, directly confirming only that the downstream exploit module was absent from its parent; it cannot establish parent absence for the external plugin flaw.

Commit-object check on the downstream-only candidate: `git cat-file commit d8c55501a52ece2e7360032c7422f95e2e595135` shows author and committer `h00die <michaeltcyr@gmail.com>`, parent a4a7efddb756c887a08780562e37f77fe199f34d, and only the subject `ait csv improter exploit`, with no AI/bot trailer. Because this object did not introduce the vulnerable handler, protocol forbids using its marker absence for an AI verdict.

Public-history boundary: both https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-q6q7-289w-x495 and the canonical duplicate advisory https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-p27j-qf57-7cm7 state `Source code: No known source code`; the assigned clone has no plugin source or plugin release commits. Consequently there is no public commit graph in which to run meaningful -S/-L attribution on upload-handler.php, verify its immediate parent, identify the 3.0.4 fixing commit, or inspect the true BIC commit object.
reasoning: The vulnerability lifecycle is externally well established: exploitation was observed on 2020-11-12, WPScan reproduced it against 3.0.3 and disclosed it on 2020-11-13, and later records place the closing version boundary at 3.0.4. CVE-2025-34083 is only a rejected duplicate of CVE-2020-36849. The Rapid7 repository entered the record because it added a working exploit module on 2021-01-01; that commit neither shipped nor fixed the vulnerable WordPress handler. Treating that module addition as the BIC would invert causality and violate the smallest-real-BIC rule. The actual proprietary plugin history is not publicly available, so the introducer, its direct parent absence, the direct fix commit, and BIC-only AI signal cannot be reconstructed. This is a genuine source-history boundary, making BLOCKED more accurate than NOT_AI or EVIDENCE_GAP.
remaining_gap: A first-party version-controlled history (or authenticated commit/export provenance) for the AIT CSV Import / Export plugin spanning the introduction of admin/upload-handler.php through releases 3.0.3 and 3.0.4 is required to identify the smallest BIC, verify its immediate parent, locate the direct fix commit, and inspect the BIC commit object for AI markers. Public release-version claims alone cannot supply commit SHAs or commit-object provenance.
